# PandaScore fixtures

No real PandaScore response has been captured yet (no API token was available when the adapter was written). Two kinds of file are here; neither is a live response, and each file says so in its own `_source` / `_constructed` key.

| File | Kind | Represents |
|---|---|---|
| `doc-example-csgo_matches-1-0.json` | Official documentation example (OpenAPI example of `GET /csgo/matches?page[size]=1`, saved 2026-11-21, unedited) | A not-started Bo3 "Grand final: TBD vs TBD" of a Playoffs tournament (`has_bracket: true`), CCT Europe 2025, with nested `serie` and `tournament`. Our "Event without a Swiss Stage" (a Playoffs-only serie). |
| `doc-example-tournaments_brackets-0.json` | Official documentation example (`GET /tournaments/1590/brackets`, unedited) | A finished Bo5 match with opponents, results 3-2, `winner_id` and `previous_matches`. It is League of Legends data (Worlds 2018): the match shape is the same across games, so it is used only to check how a finished match with teams parses. |
| `constructed-swiss-major.json` | **Constructed** (hand-built, NOT a real response) | A Major with a Swiss Stage and a Playoffs bracket: serie, two tournaments and their matches, built from the documented field shapes. Covers finished (also a forfeit), running, postponed, canceled, TBD-opponent and bracket matches. Generated by a script; teams, ids and dates are invented. |

## What is and is not verified

- Verified (against documentation only): the field names and values the parser reads (`status`, `begin_at`, `scheduled_at`, `winner_id`, `forfeit`, `match_type`, `number_of_games`, `opponents`, `results`, `previous_matches`, tournament `has_bracket`).
- **Not verified:** how PandaScore represents a real Major's Swiss Stage. The docs never mention Swiss. The parser therefore guesses a Stage is Swiss when its tournament has no bracket and its name contains "Swiss" or "Stage <n>", and derives the Swiss round and record bucket by replaying results (PandaScore has no such field). `constructed-swiss-major.json` follows that guess, so a green test only shows the parser does what we think, not that PandaScore looks like that.

## Capturing the real thing (owner, once)

With the owner's token, save (unedited, one file each) the responses of these requests for a past Major, e.g. IEM Cologne Major 2026 (header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`):

1. `GET https://api.pandascore.co/csgo/series?search[name]=Major&sort=-begin_at` to find the serie id.
2. `GET https://api.pandascore.co/series/<serie id>/tournaments`: shows how the Swiss stages and the Playoffs are named and flagged.
3. `GET https://api.pandascore.co/tournaments/<a Swiss stage tournament id>/matches`: shows whether matches carry any round information.
4. `GET https://api.pandascore.co/tournaments/<the Playoffs tournament id>/brackets`.

Also confirm that `GET /csgo/series?filter[id]=<id>`, `/csgo/series/running`, `/csgo/series/upcoming` and `range[begin_at]` on `/csgo/series` (the calls the fetch layer makes) are accepted on the free plan. Then replace `constructed-swiss-major.json` with the real files and fix the parser's Stage-kind guess.
